agent_authority_substrate.does_not_mean: This layer governs how claims ABOUT the project become canonical. It does not govern, compute, or influence any physics. Agent execution cannot directly mutate authoritative scientific state, evidence, or acceptance state except through the governed interfaces and event-derived authority machinery. No solver or scientific model imports qta_agent/, and nothing here moves an acceptance decision by itself. A record reaching PROMOTED here means a claim was proposed, independently verified, and promoted under a recorded policy -- it does not mean a gate passed, that anything was measured, or that hardware exists. Likewise a task reaching VERIFIED on the governed Stage-10 path means a declared tool ran under kernel-enforced CPU, address-space, output-size, process-count and core-dump bounds; was granted no network authority by this substrate; produced the bytes it claims; and a SEPARATED registered actor confirmed those bytes are still on disk. Those are two separate statements and only the first is the kernel's: none of the rlimits restricts networking, a child process can open sockets, and what is withheld is authority rather than capability. The in-process socket guard is a monkeypatch in the parent interpreter and is not containment; it does not exist in a child at all. That is provenance. It is not scientific validity.
agent_authority_substrate.note: Enforcement is verified by mutation testing rather than by coverage: each check is deleted in turn and the suite must fail. tools/mutation_matrix.py exits non-zero on a survivor, on an anchor that no longer matches its source, on a source not restored byte-identically, on collateral damage to a tracked file, or on a post-run baseline that no longer passes; it refuses to start against a red baseline OR a non-deterministic one. The harness is itself mutated by tools/mutations/mutation_harness.json, after a defect was found in it: it could run a mutation against the PREVIOUS mutation's cached bytecode whenever both changed the file by the same number of bytes within one mtime second, which reported kills for mutations nothing had tested. A second harness defect was found the same way: its collateral-damage restore is 'git checkout HEAD --', which cannot tell a suite-damaged file from an uncommitted edit, and it destroyed real work twice in one session; the restore still happens and the discarded bytes are now kept under .mutation-quarantine/. A surviving mutation means a check is unprotected, not that it is redundant. Mutation testing asks whether a check that EXISTS is load-bearing; it cannot ask whether one is MISSING, because there is nothing to delete. Two techniques cover that: Hypothesis state machines over the authority, task and job machines, and a hostile-agent campaign against the governed path. Each found defects the other could not -- the campaign found the task replay re-authorizing a forged record against the starting state the record itself declared, which let one appended line move a task out of the sealed VERIFIED state. Narrative form: AGENT_SUBSTRATE.md; per-requirement status: docs/completion_matrix.json.
agent_authority_substrate.status: BUILT_AND_VERIFIED_WITH_ONE_PRODUCTION_CALLER: qta_agent/governed_stage10.py is invoked by the Snakefile's s10_governed rule, so the substrate has a consumer that does real work and writes files somebody reads. tests/test_agent_substrate_isolation.py enforces the narrow, named crossing that permits it (two bridge modules reaching one thing, the Stage-10 write guard) and still forbids the other direction absolutely. What has NOT changed: nothing scientific has been promoted through this layer. No existing claim, gate, document, or canonical output has been re-derived under it, and PROMOTED in the authority state machine remains a state reached only in tests. The governed workflow is ONE workflow, of the safest available kind -- artifact generation with automatic_gate_effect=NONE -- and the ungoverned Stage-10 adapters remain directly callable, so the governed path is additive rather than the only route. Governing a claim, a gate or a canonical output is a separate change that must name which claims it governs and who holds each role.
